name: ObjectMerge
summary: Keeps a record that turned out to be a duplicate and points it at the one now in use, so that references made before the merge still resolve.

roles.name: ActiveObject
roles.summary: The record now in use, and the one everything should reach. Figure 5.5 makes it a «dynamic» subtype, which is right: no record is created active as opposed to superseded, it simply has not been merged away yet.

roles.name: SupersededObject
roles.summary: A record found to be the same thing as another, kept rather than deleted. Deleting is the obvious move and it breaks everything that already referred to it — an invoice, an appointment, a printed letter with a number on it. What the annotation licenses is the rule that matters: a reference to one of these must resolve forward, and a query that reads it directly is reading a record the business no longer believes.

roles.name: ObjectEssence
roles.summary: The thing itself, holding its several appearances. Figure 5.6 is the other shape the section gives, and it suits a model that never knew which record was primary: instead of one record absorbing another, both remain appearances of one essence. A model uses this or the active-superseded pair, not both.
